armor.name: Model 100 Vest
armor.special_desc: DISCRETE (You hardly register on electronic surveillance. You now always have passive concealment of 5 vs AI and Electronics.)
armor.desc: The Model 100 is the catalog's idea of corporate dignity: a flat slab of armoured cloth you can pull on under a work shirt and forget about. It offers only token protection against blades, bullets, beams, or the occult alike, which is to say it will spoil a mugger's afternoon and very little else. Its real selling point is the woven dampening lining that smears your electronic signature into static, so cameras and watchful systems file you under nobody worth a second look. You'll find one in any market, priced for a mid-level employee's monthly stipend, and worn by roughly that many. It is, in the end, less a suit of armour than a polite request to be left alone.

armor.name: Model 440 Vest
armor.special_desc: DISCRETE (You hardly register on electronic surveillance. You now always have passive concealment of 5 vs AI and Electronics.), OPT (Item can have 1 compatible option of any kind)
armor.desc: A step up from the entry tier, the Model 440 trades a little of the featureless calm for actual stopping power against knives and slugs, taking the edge off a beating that would have folded its cheaper cousin. It keeps the same quiet lining that leaves you all but invisible to scanners, so you stay both harder to hurt and harder to notice. There is room for a single custom modification, which is exactly the sort of detail that lets a buyer pretend it was a considered purchase rather than a nervous one. The pattern began as a BMS design, though what reaches the rack is the unbranded license, the same cut without the proprietary lining tricks that earned the name. It is the vest people buy after the first incident, not before, and against energy, hacking, or anything that whispers from the dark, you're still mostly on your own.

armor.name: Hazard Suit
armor.special_desc: INNOCULATION (Device protects against non lethal environmental hazards. Gain a LARGE bonus to skills rolls against lethal environmental hazards and ailments.)
armor.desc: The Hazard Suit is built for environments that want you dead by chemistry rather than by violence, and it is honest about that division of labor. Against blades and bullets it offers little, but its sealed weave and onboard filtration shrug off toxins, contagion, and the slow creep of intrusion, while lending a real edge against even the lethal hazards that would otherwise pickle a careless body. The faint resistance it shows to spiritual harm is a happy accident of all that insulating bulk, not a marketing claim. Found on any industrial world and reasonably priced, it is the garment colonists and salvage crews swear by and tourists never think to pack. Wear it where the air itself is the enemy; wear something else where the people are.

armor.name: Pilot Gear
armor.special_desc: SPACE (Device is rated for space and provides up to 8 hours of life support as well as magnetic boots. Treat character as having GRAVITY TRAINING when walking on compatible surfaces.)
armor.desc: Pilot Gear is the unglamorous flight suit every cockpit jockey owns and nobody photographs, padded just enough to take the edge off a rough landing and nothing more. Against any serious weapon it is barely better than a thick coat, which the manufacturers will cheerfully admit if you read past the first page. Its genuine virtue is the rating that keeps you breathing in vacuum for the better part of a shift, plus magnetic boots that let you stroll a hull like the floor was a personal favor. Cheap and stocked at any port worth the name, it is one of those purchases you only regret not making once. The void does not negotiate, and this is the suit that lets you ignore it for eight hours.

armor.name: Kevmail jacket
armor.special_desc: UNIVERSAL (Device can fit any of the alliance races, in the case of ARMOR, it can be put on or removed as a COMPLEX action), OPT (Item can have 1 compatible option of any kind)
armor.desc: The Kevmail jacket is the urban survivor's standby, a layered weave that looks like a workaday coat and absorbs a solid beating from blades and bullets like one several grades nicer. It fits every Alliance physiology without a tailor's fuss and comes off in a hurry when the situation demands, which is more often than the catalog implies. There's room for a single custom modification, so owners can fool themselves into thinking it was the bespoke choice. Mass-produced and stocked in any market at a price that respects a working wage, it has dressed more cautious commuters than anyone cares to count. It will not stop a beam or a hacker, but it was never pretending to.

armor.name: Series 1040
armor.special_desc: SMUGGLER (Can hide up to a small object. Provides passive concealment of 5 or a LARGE bonus to an active Concealment roll.)
armor.desc: The Series 1040 is for people who carry things they'd rather not explain at a checkpoint. Beneath its respectable cut it offers solid protection against physical harm and a creditable buffer against intrusion, but the real engineering went into the hidden compartment that swallows a small object and the dampening that lets you walk past inspection looking like you've nothing to hide. Investigators and bounty hunters favor it precisely because it does two jobs and admits to neither. It costs more than its protection alone would justify and turns up only at the better-stocked outfitters. You're paying for the pocket, and everyone in the trade knows it.

armor.name: A1000 Frontier coat
armor.special_desc: INSULATING (Always get maximum SOAK rolls when defending against ENERGY attacks.)
armor.desc: The A1000 Frontier coat is the garment you buy when the sky itself is trying to cook you. Its layered insulation gives respectable protection against blades and bullets, but it truly comes alive against energy, reliably drinking down pulse, thermal, and plasma at the very top of what its weave can manage, as though daring the universe to try harder. Frontier prospectors and edge-world haulers prize it for surviving solar flare and weapon-flash with the same shrug. It is expensive and hard to come by, which suits the sort of people who wear one just fine. Tech and the occult slip right past it, but out where this coat earns its keep, those are tomorrow's problems.

armor.name: Balistic Vest
armor.special_desc: UNIVERSAL (Device can fit any of the alliance races, in the case of ARMOR, it can be put on or removed as a COMPLEX action), OPT (Item can have 1 compatible option of any kind)
armor.desc: The Balistic Vest is exactly what the unglamorous name promises: a no-nonsense slab of plating that fits any Alliance frame and offers solid protection against blades and bullets, with nothing left over for anything fancier. It absorbs less of a beating than its weight suggests, so think of it as insurance against the first shot rather than the fifth. It accepts a single custom modification, which is the only concession it makes to ambition. Pricier than its bare numbers warrant and only stocked at decent outfitters, it sells largely on the comfort of the word 'ballistic' stamped across the chest. Practical, honest, and just slightly overcharged.

armor.name: Field Vest
armor.special_desc: HARDENED (Always get maximum SOAK rolls when defending against PHYSICAL attacks.)
armor.desc: The Field Vest is built around one stubborn promise: when something physical hits you, it gives the very best it has, every single time, no luck involved. That reliability against blades and bullets makes it a favorite of people who've learned that a merely average layer is the one that fails at the worst moment. Against beams, intrusion, or the occult it offers only the thinnest courtesy, so don't mistake its consistency for range. It costs a bit more than a basic vest and turns up at the better suppliers rather than the corner stall. For close, dirty work where the threat is a fist or a knife, few things this cheap behave so dependably.

armor.name: Street Jacket
armor.special_desc: DISCRETE (You hardly register on electronic surveillance. You now always have passive concealment of 5 vs AI and Electronics.), OPT (Item can have 1 compatible option of any kind)
armor.desc: The Street Jacket is the pattern at the top of its game, a deceptively casual piece that takes a serious beating from blades and bullets while looking like something you'd wear to be seen in. The same lining that armours you also smears your signature off the grid, so you read to cameras and systems as nobody worth flagging. It leaves room for a single custom modification, which most owners use and all owners mention. The cut was a Harsh original, though the version on the shelf is the generic copy that spread once the look caught on, handsome enough without the house finishing that carried the label. Beams and hackers still bother it, but on a crowded street, not being seen is the better protection anyway.

armor.name: Spiritweave vest
armor.special_desc: SPIRITPROOF (Always get maximum SOAK rolls when defending against SPIRITUAL attacks.)
armor.desc: The Spiritweave vest is for the unusual clientele who've concluded that bullets are the least of their worries. Its threads are wound through with materials that meet the occult head-on, giving its formidable utmost against spiritual assault every time, while also turning a respectable shoulder to energy. Against ordinary blades it is merely adequate, a fact its makers consider beside the point. Costly and seldom seen for sale, it surfaces mostly in the hands of exorcists, mystics, and people who have seen something they refuse to describe. If you don't already know why you'd need one, you probably don't; if you do, nothing else will do.

armor.name: Heavy mesh Vest
armor.special_desc: UNIVERSAL (Device can fit any of the alliance races, in the case of ARMOR, it can be put on or removed as a COMPLEX action), OPT (Item can have 1 compatible option of any kind)
armor.desc: The Heavy mesh Vest is the affordable workhorse of mid-weight protection, a dense interlock that fits any Alliance body and shrugs off a fair beating from both blades and beams without complaint. It strikes the comfortable middle ground, decent against the physical and decent against energy, asking little and forgiving much. There's room for a single custom modification, and it shucks on and off without ceremony when the day turns. Stocked in any market and priced like the practical purchase it is, it's the vest that quietly outfits half the working security on any given world. No frills, no surprises, just an honest layer between you and the usual trouble.

armor.name: Security Suit
armor.special_desc: DUELIST (Always get maximum SOAK rolls when defending against MELEE attacks.), OPT (Item can have 1 compatible option of any kind)
armor.desc: The Security Suit is corporate-guard standard for a reason: it absorbs a genuinely heavy beating from blades and bullets, buffers intrusion respectably, and gives its very best whenever someone closes to knife range, every time without fail. That last trait makes it the terror of breakroom duelists and the comfort of anyone who works the kind of shift where conversations end in steel. It takes a single custom modification, which most departments quietly standardize across a roster. Easy enough to find anywhere and priced for a security budget rather than a hero's, it is the suit you've already been shot at by, whether you knew it or not. Dependable, unglamorous, and very good at its narrow job.

armor.name: Light Infantry
armor.special_desc: OPT (Item can have 1 compatible option of any kind)
armor.desc: Light Infantry armour is the unusually honest generalist, offering solid, even-handed protection against blades, beams, intrusion, and the occult in equal measure, refusing to specialize in anything except not letting you down. It absorbs a healthy beating across the board, which is exactly what you want when you can't predict which flavor of trouble arrives first. A single custom modification lets a unit tune it toward whatever the briefing implies. Mass-produced for standing forces and priced like the bulk-order staple it is, it turns up in any market without fuss. It is never the best answer to a specific threat, and almost always a sensible answer to an unknown one.

armor.name: Infiltration Gear
armor.special_desc: STEALTH (Device is designed for covert ops and provides a SMALL bonus to CONCEALMENT rolls.), OPT (Item can have 1 compatible option of any kind)
armor.desc: Infiltration Gear makes a deliberate trade most armour wouldn't dare: it barely takes the edge off a blade, on the theory that if you're being hit, the mission has already gone wrong. What it does brilliantly is keep you unseen, buffering intrusion and the occult while lending a real hand to staying tucked in the shadows where you belong. Cut for ghosts and tailored for people who'd rather not be seen, it takes a single custom modification for whatever the job requires. It runs expensive and stocks only at specialist suppliers, who never ask what you intend. Wear it to slip past a problem, never to win a fight with one.

armor.name: Darkspace Survivor VI
armor.special_desc: SPACE (Device is rated for space and provides up to 8 hours of life support as well as magnetic boots. Treat character as having GRAVITY TRAINING when walking on compatible surfaces.), INNOCULATION (Device protects against non lethal environmental hazards. Gain a LARGE bonus to skills rolls against lethal environmental hazards and ailments.)
armor.desc: The Darkspace Survivor VI is built for the long, cold places where the environment kills you slower and stranger than any gun. It is rated for vacuum with hours of life support and magnetic boots, and its sealed weave fends off the lethal hazards of the deep black while turning a respectable shoulder to energy and the occult. Against blades it is unremarkable, because out where it earns its keep, almost nothing is holding a blade. Expensive and hard to find, it's the suit deep-salvage crews and frontier wanderers trust when home is a long way off and getting longer. It will not make the dark friendly, only survivable.

armor.name: Recon suit
armor.special_desc: STEALTH (Device is designed for covert ops and provides a SMALL bonus to CONCEALMENT rolls.), OPT (Item can have 1 compatible option of any kind)
armor.desc: The Recon suit is a whisper to the surveillance state, built around an excellent buffer against intrusion and hacking that no signal seems quite able to bite into. Against physical harm it is thin, a deliberate choice for a garment meant to gather information rather than win arguments. It also helps you stay tucked out of sight, cut for the sort of work where being noticed is the only real failure. A single custom modification rounds it out for the specifics of a job. Pricier than its armour suggests and stocked only by outfitters who cater to watchers and the watched, it sells entirely on what it keeps out of other people's systems.

armor.name: Nano Ablative
armor.special_desc: NANOBOTS (During maintenance phase you can spend any number of NANITES to reroll failed AILMENTS saves.), HEALING (During MAINTENANCE you can spend any number of NANITES, or personal CHI to recover an equal amount of HEALTH or MORALE)
armor.desc: Nano Ablative is what happens when armour is built to fight back. Its surface is a seething skin of machines that gives excellent, formidable protection against blades and bullets, flaking away under impact and rebuilding between the violence. The same swarm scrubs ailments from your blood and knits health and morale back together when you take a moment to let it work. It is genuinely expensive and far from easy to find, the kind of suit that quietly tells the room you're hard to put down and harder to keep down. Against beams, hackers, and the occult it offers little, but the things it's good at, it is very good at indeed.

armor.name: Ghost Mesh
armor.special_desc: STEALTH (Device is designed for covert ops and provides a SMALL bonus to CONCEALMENT rolls.), PHASE (Phase you out of reality when attacked. Gain a 1 in 10 chance of negating any attack.)
armor.desc: Ghost Mesh is for operators who'd rather the universe forget they were ever there, and it obliges with unsettling literalness. Beyond solid, balanced protection against blades, beams, and the occult, it keeps you tucked out of sight, and at the worst moment it can flicker you a half-step out of reality entirely, so an attack that should have landed simply finds nobody home. That trick is fickle and unreliable by design, but the once it saves you tends to be the once that mattered. It is very expensive and genuinely hard to source, the province of specialists who don't list references. Wear it to be somewhere, and occasionally, to have never been.

armor.name: Bioweave Armor
armor.special_desc: UNIVERSAL (Device can fit any of the alliance races, in the case of ARMOR, it can be put on or removed as a COMPLEX action), MASTERWORK (Critical hits have no additional effects. Masterwork has no effect if the wearer is BREACHED.)
armor.desc: Bioweave Armor is a living lattice grown rather than stitched, fitting any Alliance physiology like a second skin and coming off as easily. Its protection against blades, beams, and the occult is solid and balanced, but it absorbs less raw punishment than its price implies, because its true craft lies elsewhere. The cultured weave blunts the cruelty of a critical hit, turning what should be a maiming into merely a wound, provided your protection hasn't already been breached. The technique was pioneered in the Malivaux labs, but this is the generic strain that propagated once the method got out, the same living craft without the signed refinements of the branded original. You buy it not to take more hits, but to survive the one that would have ended someone cheaper.

armor.name: Nerulian Ghostplate
armor.special_desc: SPIRITPROOF (Always get maximum SOAK rolls when defending against SPIRITUAL attacks.), PHASE (Phase you out of reality when attacked. Gain a 1 in 10 chance of negating any attack.)
armor.desc: The Nerulian Ghostplate is less a product than a legend with an owner, a one-of-its-kind relic whose origins nobody fully agrees on. It meets the occult with its very best every time and balances respectable cover across blades, beams, and the unseen besides, but its signature is the way it can blink you out of reality at the instant of harm, letting an attack pass through the space you just vacated. Such a thing is functionally impossible to find and priced beyond all but the obscenely wealthy or the obscenely lucky. Those who've worn it speak of it the way people speak of a near-death they didn't quite have. There is exactly one conversation worth having about acquiring it, and it ends with you not affording it.

armor.name: Fringe Fat-B
armor.special_desc: BUNKER (Always get maximum SOAK rolls when not moving. (Bonus applies during maintenance phase after a full round of no movement).), OPT (Item can have 1 compatible option of any kind)
armor.desc: The Fringe Fat-B is a frontier improviser's masterpiece, an ungainly slab that turns excellent, formidable protection against energy into its whole personality. Stand still and it does its best work, drinking down pulse and plasma at full measure the moment you stop moving and dig in, which suits the dug-in sort of fight it was made for. It manages solid cover against blades and a fair shoulder to the occult besides, though tech threats slide right by. A single custom modification lets owners adapt it to whatever the standoff requires. Costly and hard to find out past the well-mapped lanes, it's the armour of people who've decided the best way through a firefight is to become furniture and wait.

armor.name: Baer Armor
armor.special_desc: POWERED (Armor no longer reduces CARRYING CAPACITY but you now have a SMALL penalty to PHYSICAL and ACUITY SKILL checks. POWERED Armors are always Extra Large when not worn and count as ELECTRONICS vs EMP. ), DUELIST (Always get maximum SOAK rolls when defending against MELEE attacks.)
armor.desc: Baer Armor is a powered exoskeleton dressed as a suit, carrying its own considerable weight so you don't have to, at the modest cost of making you a touch clumsier in the fine motions. It offers excellent, formidable protection against blades and bullets and a respectable answer to beams, intrusion, and the occult alike, a genuinely well-rounded shell. Close to melee range it gives its very best every time, which makes its wearers fearless in a brawl and insufferable about it. The downside is candid in the spec: powered and electronic, it dislikes anything that fries circuits, and it is bulky and awkward off the body. Expensive and seldom seen on the open market, it's the suit you wear when you intend to be the heaviest thing in the room.

armor.name: Series 9000
armor.special_desc: SMUGGLER (Can hide up to a small object. Provides passive concealment of 5 or a LARGE bonus to an active Concealment roll.), OPT (Item can have 1 compatible option of any kind)
armor.desc: The Series 9000 is the flagship of the discerning sneak, a well-rounded shell that turns solid, balanced protection against blades, beams, intrusion, and the occult into a respectable all-day garment. Its real artistry is the concealed compartment that swallows a small object whole, paired with dampening that lets you carry it past any inspection looking utterly unremarkable. A single custom modification rounds it out for whatever line of work demands such discretion. It is expensive and hard to find, sold quietly to investigators, couriers, and others who measure success by what nobody noticed. You pay for the protection and the secret pocket, but mostly, everyone understands, for the pocket.

armor.name: Grisly Armor
armor.special_desc: SERVOS (Your PHYSICAL attribute for MIGHT checks is 10. Device now counts as ELECTRONIC Vs EMP.), DUELIST (Always get maximum SOAK rolls when defending against MELEE attacks.)
armor.desc: The Grisly was conceived for soldiers who treat a melee scrum as a recreational activity. The frame is a snarl of servo-assisted plating that lets even a featherweight wearer throw a punch like a loading mech, and the joints are tuned so it laughs off pulse weapons that fry lesser kit. Against blades and bullets it offers excellent protection, absorbing close-quarters punishment with a kind of insulting ease, and a duelist locked inside one rarely loses a knife fight. Energy weapons earn respect rather than terror, while hacking and the occult barely register on the design brief at all. It can be found if you know who to ask, and you will pay for the privilege of looking this menacing.

armor.name: Heavy Infantry
armor.special_desc: OPT (Item can have 1 compatible option of any kind)
armor.desc: The Heavy Infantry is the sensible choice for people who expect to be shot with light, and the reputation is not wrong. Its plating is layered to shrug off pulse and thermal fire with formidable confidence, while blades, bullets, intrusion attempts, and the occult all meet merely respectable resistance, the design splitting its attention evenly rather than excelling at any one thing. It is not the toughest shell on the rack, but it carries itself with the unbothered competence of gear that has survived countless field reviews. There is room for a single custom modification, which most quartermasters fill before the suit even reaches the wearer. You can lay hands on one without much trouble, though the cost reminds you it was never meant for civilians.

armor.name: Blockade Armor
armor.special_desc: BUNKER (Always get maximum SOAK rolls when not moving. (Bonus applies during maintenance phase after a full round of no movement).), INDESTRUCTIBLE (This defense cannot be BREACHED.)
armor.desc: The Blockade does exactly what its name promises and very little it does not. Stand your ground in one and it becomes a small fortress, its already excellent absorption tightening into something that simply refuses to be moved or undone, and no attack has ever managed to crack the shell open. Across blades, energy, intrusion, and the occult it offers solid, even-handed protection, the work of designers who decided that being unbreakable mattered more than being specialized. The catch, naturally, is that all that immovability rewards the patient and punishes the sprinter. It can be sourced from the right depot, at a price that assumes you intend to plant your feet and stay a while.

armor.name: Sec-Tac Vanguard
armor.special_desc: HARDENED (Always get maximum SOAK rolls when defending against PHYSICAL attacks.), INSULATING (Always get maximum SOAK rolls when defending against ENERGY attacks.)
armor.desc: The Sec-Tac pattern was bred for the moment when both bullets and pulse fire arrive at once, and the Vanguard handles that reunion with grim poise. Its plating is hardened against blades and bullets and insulated against energy in equal measure, turning aside physical and thermal punishment with formidable, maximum-effort consistency. Hacking it is more plausible than the rest of its resume suggests, and the occult was clearly an afterthought, but a frontline trooper rarely loses sleep over either. It absorbs a beating and stands there waiting for the next one, which is precisely the personality riot-line work demands. Stocked widely enough through security channels, though the asking figure is firmly in corporate-budget territory.

armor.name: Robocop
armor.special_desc: POWERED (Armor no longer reduces CARRYING CAPACITY but you now have a SMALL penalty to PHYSICAL and ACUITY SKILL checks. POWERED Armors are always Extra Large when not worn and count as ELECTRONICS vs EMP. ), UNIVERSAL (Device can fit any of the alliance races, in the case of ARMOR, it can be put on or removed as a COMPLEX action)
armor.desc: The Robocop is the answer to the eternal grievance of heavy armor, which is that it weighs as much as a guilty conscience. Powered servos carry the load for you, so the bulk no longer drags at your back, at the modest cost of a little clumsiness in fine movement and acuity. The plating delivers excellent protection against blades and bullets, respectable cover against energy and intrusion, and frankly nothing for the occult. It is shaped to fit any of the Alliance races and can be climbed into or shucked off in a single deliberate effort, which is a mercy given that out of the suit it is an enormous, awkward heap. Stocked in just about any market and, by powered-armor standards, almost suspiciously affordable.

armor.name: Tactical Suit
armor.special_desc: STEALTH (Device is designed for covert ops and provides a SMALL bonus to CONCEALMENT rolls.), HACKPROOF (Always get maximum SOAK rolls when defending against TECH attacks.)
armor.desc: The Tactical Suit is for operators who want to be heavily armored and entirely unbothered by anyone with a keyboard. No intrusion has ever gotten through its shell, and it is cut for ghosts, tailored to slip a bulky frame past notice better than any heavy rig has a right to. It gives excellent protection against blades, bullets, and hacking alike, though it skimps badly on energy and the occult, trusting you to not get caught in a firefight you cannot end quickly. The trade-off is the eye-watering cost and the difficulty of finding one outside specialist channels. For the right covert contract, frontline buyers consider it worth every credit they would rather not discuss.

armor.name: Starship Trooper
armor.special_desc: SPACE (Device is rated for space and provides up to 8 hours of life support as well as magnetic boots. Treat character as having GRAVITY TRAINING when walking on compatible surfaces.), INSULATING (Always get maximum SOAK rolls when defending against ENERGY attacks.)
armor.desc: Built for the kind of fight that happens where there is no air to scream into, the Starship Trooper is a shell rated for hard vacuum. It carries the better part of a working day's life support and magnetic boots that let the wearer stride across a hull as though gravity had simply agreed to cooperate. The plating insulates superbly against pulse and plasma and resists intrusion with formidable confidence, while blades and bullets meet solid cover and the occult meets a shrug. It absorbs energy fire with the steady patience of something designed to take a beating in places nobody can hear it. Genuinely hard to come by, and priced for fleets rather than freelancers.

armor.name: Assault Gear
armor.special_desc: SERVOS (Your PHYSICAL attribute for MIGHT checks is 10. Device now counts as ELECTRONIC Vs EMP.), MASTERWORK (Critical hits have no additional effects. Masterwork has no effect if the wearer is BREACHED.)
armor.desc: The Assault Gear is a servo-driven breaching shell for troopers who go through the door first and expect to be shot for it from both barrels. The frame lends a slight wearer the strength of a loader, and excellent protection against both blades and bullets and pulse and plasma means it walks into crossfire that would shred lesser kit. Better still, the build smooths away the cruel little flourishes that turn a clean hit into a crippling one, at least until the shell itself is finally cracked. Hacking and the occult get the bare minimum of attention, which suits a soldier whose problems are loud and immediate. It is a hard find and a harder invoice, the kind of gear that arrives crated with a contract attached.

armor.name: Xenotrium Assault
armor.special_desc: INDESTRUCTIBLE (This defense cannot be BREACHED.), MASTERWORK (Critical hits have no additional effects. Masterwork has no effect if the wearer is BREACHED.)
armor.desc: Forged around an alloy nobody fully explains, the Xenotrium Assault is built to absorb a punishing beating and ask politely for seconds. Its shell simply cannot be cracked open, and the workmanship is fine enough besides to deny critical strikes the vicious extra bite they crave, so long as it holds together. Pulse and plasma fire meets formidable insulation, while blades, intrusion, and the occult all run into solid, evenly distributed resistance. There is nothing flashy in its profile; it is the dependable wall that outlasts the people shooting at it. Genuinely hard to track down and expensive enough to make a quartermaster wince, it is the sort of investment you make once and bury people in.

armor.name: Sen Tao
armor.special_desc: BUNKER (Always get maximum SOAK rolls when not moving. (Bonus applies during maintenance phase after a full round of no movement).), DUELIST (Always get maximum SOAK rolls when defending against MELEE attacks.)
armor.desc: The Sen Tao is a curiously elegant piece of heavy plate, an interpretation of the bunker philosophy for buyers who refuse to choose between dueling and dug-in resilience. Plant your feet and its protection tightens to its absolute maximum, and woe to anyone who closes to blade range, where it turns aside melee with the same flawless consistency. It pairs excellent cover against blades and bullets with formidable resistance to intrusion, respectable shielding against energy and the occult, and a frame that rewards stillness over sprinting. The design first came off a Malivaux bench, but this is the unbranded reproduction of that pattern, the elegant silhouette without the bespoke fitting that justified the original's name. Distinctly hard to find on any market, and priced like the object it imitates.

armor.name: Gut master
armor.special_desc: POWERED (Armor no longer reduces CARRYING CAPACITY but you now have a SMALL penalty to PHYSICAL and ACUITY SKILL checks. POWERED Armors are always Extra Large when not worn and count as ELECTRONICS vs EMP. ), DUELIST (Always get maximum SOAK rolls when defending against MELEE attacks.)
armor.desc: The Gut Master is honest about its priorities, which is to say it would like very much to be in a knife fight. Powered servos haul its considerable bulk so the weight stops being your problem, costing you only a touch of finesse in exchange, and against anyone foolish enough to close to melee it turns aside blows with flawless, maximum-effort reliability. It gives excellent protection against blades and bullets and respectable cover against energy, while hacking and the occult slide right off the design brief. It does not absorb the heaviest sustained punishment, trusting the wearer to end disputes at arm's length before that matters. Hard to track down and far from cheap, though brawlers swear the investment pays for itself in won arguments.

armor.name: Dilythium Mail
armor.special_desc: HARDENED (Always get maximum SOAK rolls when defending against PHYSICAL attacks.), OPT (Item can have 1 compatible option of any kind)
armor.desc: Dilythium Mail is what happens when heavy armor is built to also be a flex. Its layered weave absorbs a frankly absurd beating, the densest absorption on most racks, and against blades and bullets it locks to its maximum every single time. Pulse and plasma fire meets formidable insulation, while intrusion and the occult run into solid, respectable resistance across the board. It also leaves room for a single custom modification, in case six layers of exotic alloy somehow felt insufficient to you. Production is tightly rationed and the price is openly ridiculous, which is rather the point, since you do not wear Dilythium to blend in.

armor.name: Skalander Godplate
armor.special_desc: DUELIST (Always get maximum SOAK rolls when defending against MELEE attacks.), SPIRITPROOF (Always get maximum SOAK rolls when defending against SPIRITUAL attacks.)
armor.desc: Skalander Godplate comes wrapped in frontier legend, and its makers do nothing to discourage the stories. Beyond excellent protection against blades and bullets, it is one of the few heavy shells that takes the occult seriously, warding off spiritual assault with the same flawless, maximum-effort certainty it brings to a melee clash, where no blade finds a clean opening. Energy fire meets respectable resistance and hacking is largely ignored, which tells you what kind of enemies the original wearers feared most. It absorbs a heavy beating and carries itself like a relic that fully expects to outlive you. Production is strictly rationed and the cost is monstrous, fitting for plate that half its owners insist is blessed.

armor.name: Titan Defender
armor.special_desc: SPACE (Device is rated for space and provides up to 8 hours of life support as well as magnetic boots. Treat character as having GRAVITY TRAINING when walking on compatible surfaces.), NANOBOTS (During maintenance phase you can spend any number of NANITES to reroll failed AILMENTS saves.)
armor.desc: The Titan Defender is a vacuum-rated workhorse for crews who expect the void itself to try and kill them in creative ways. It supplies most of a working day of life support and magnetic boots that make hull-walking feel routine, while a lattice of repair-minded machines lets the wearer shrug off poisons, burns, and lingering afflictions that would fell a lesser trooper. Its plating insulates superbly against pulse and plasma and resists intrusion with formidable confidence, with solid cover against blades and bullets and little patience for the occult. It absorbs a serious beating and quietly mends what slips through. Scarce in supply and priced for serious operations, it is the suit you wear when survival, not style, is the entire mission.

armor.name: Wraith
armor.special_desc: CLOAK (Provides passive CONCEALMENT 3 type I and II. Passive concealment is 6 when not moving for a round.), STEALTH (Device is designed for covert ops and provides a SMALL bonus to CONCEALMENT rolls.)
armor.desc: The Wraith is heavy armor that has somehow learned to disappear, which ought to be impossible and is exactly why it costs what it does. It bends scanners and sightlines around itself, all but invisible when still and merely very hard to spot when moving, and it is cut for ghosts on top of that, layering misdirection over misdirection. Defensively it is the even hand, offering solid, balanced protection against blades, energy, intrusion, and the occult alike while excelling at none, since its real specialty is not being there when the shot arrives. It absorbs a respectable beating for the unusual occasion the wearer is actually spotted. Strictly rationed, brutally expensive, and beloved by people who would rather you never knew they wore armor at all.

armor.name: Reaper
armor.special_desc: POWERED (Armor no longer reduces CARRYING CAPACITY but you now have a SMALL penalty to PHYSICAL and ACUITY SKILL checks. POWERED Armors are always Extra Large when not worn and count as ELECTRONICS vs EMP. ), SPACE (Device is rated for space and provides up to 8 hours of life support as well as magnetic boots. Treat character as having GRAVITY TRAINING when walking on compatible surfaces.)
armor.desc: The Reaper is the suit you read about in after-action reports filed by the survivors, of which there are pleasingly few on the other side. A powered frame carries its monstrous bulk effortlessly, it is rated for hard vacuum with a full shift of life support and hull-walking boots, and it offers excellent protection against blades, bullets, pulse, plasma, and intrusion all at once. It absorbs a punishing beating, among the heaviest any shell can absorb, and asks for more with the bored confidence of a thing that has never lost. Only the occult slips past its attention, which is a problem for a different kind of enemy. There is essentially one of these to be had anywhere, and the price tag reads like a clerical error.

armor.name: Valkyrie
armor.special_desc: POWERED (Armor no longer reduces CARRYING CAPACITY but you now have a SMALL penalty to PHYSICAL and ACUITY SKILL checks. POWERED Armors are always Extra Large when not worn and count as ELECTRONICS vs EMP. ), AEGIS (Special modifiers to damage or power (DEADLY, DP, AS, AR and EMP etc) have no effect Vs this armor. Treat all damage at its base value.)
armor.desc: The Valkyrie is the rarest sort of heavy armor, the kind that simply declines to acknowledge the clever tricks built into a weapon. Armor-piercing rounds, deadly modifiers, intrusion spikes and worse all strike it and quietly resolve to nothing special, every hit reduced to its plain base value as though the suit had never heard of cheating. A powered frame carries its weight so the bulk never slows you, and it pairs excellent protection against blades, bullets, and the occult with respectable cover against energy and hacking. It absorbs a tremendous beating, the work of plate that treats violence as a formality. There is only one to be found, and its price belongs in legend rather than any honest ledger.

armor.name: Riot Force Shield
armor.special_desc: DEFLECTOR (Forcefield can only be used when you succeed a PARRY against ranged or melee attacks. This FORCEFIELD never needs to RECHARGE and only counts as your DEFENSE option if you succeed your PARRY.)
armor.desc: This is the answer to a crowd that has stopped asking politely. The Riot is a slab of hardened light strapped to the forearm, and it only flares when you read the strike coming and turn into it at the right instant. Time the block and the field is there, slapping aside a baton, a thrown bottle, or a slug with brutal certainty against blunt force and steel. There is no reservoir to drain and nothing to recharge, which is the whole pitch, but it does nothing at all for the slow and the surprised. It shrugs off pulse and the occult far less gracefully, which is to say only when you've already done the hard work of seeing the blow. Not hard to find, if you know which fence to ask.

armor.name: Assault Barricade
armor.special_desc: DEFLECTOR (Forcefield can only be used when you succeed a PARRY against ranged or melee attacks. This FORCEFIELD never needs to RECHARGE and only counts as your DEFENSE option if you succeed your PARRY.), NOVA (Once per SCENE as a FREE action, when this forcefield breaks you can chose to deal 2D + 4 [HIGH] STUN PHYSICAL damage to everyone in a 2m radius. Targets hit by this attack are pushed back 2m.)
armor.desc: The Barricade is for the people who breach the door first and apologize never. Like its lesser cousins it only ignites on a clean read of the incoming attack, but when it does, it eats blades, rounds, and a thermal lance with equal, excellent indifference. No power cell to babysit, no cooldown to sweat. The trick everyone buys it for: once a scene, when the field finally cracks under a hit, you can let it go out in a percussive thump that knocks everyone within a couple of meters back on their heels, slightly stunned and very reconsidering. Tech intrusion and stranger forces it merely keeps at arm's length. You'll wait a while for one to surface, and pay for the privilege.

armor.name: Combat Bulwark
armor.special_desc: DEFLECTOR (Forcefield can only be used when you succeed a PARRY against ranged or melee attacks. This FORCEFIELD never needs to RECHARGE and only counts as your DEFENSE option if you succeed your PARRY.), AEGIS (Special modifiers to damage or power (DEADLY, DP, AS, AR and EMP etc) have no effect Vs this armor. Treat all damage at its base value.)
armor.desc: There are a handful of these in known space, and nobody will confirm the count nor lower the price. The Bulwark is parry-gated like all its kind, demanding you meet the blow head-on, but what it delivers in that moment is the closest thing to a personal wall the trade has produced: excellent against steel, against energy, even against the things that whisper at the edge of the occult. Its signature is contempt for cleverness. Armor-piercing tricks, lethal little modifiers, the frying static of a hostile pulse, all of it gets flattened to plain unembellished damage before the field even notices. Its one blind spot is intrusion, where a patient hacker fares better than a battering ram. One of a kind, and it knows.

armor.name: Personal Deflector
armor.desc: The honest beginner's bubble, sold by the crate across Alliance Space because it does exactly what the label promises and nothing it doesn't. A soft envelope of standing light wraps you and holds for two good hits before it pops, knitting itself back together a breath later in time for the next exchange. Protection is even and unremarkable across the board: minimal cushioning against everything, which means it loves stopping a pistol bolt and merely tolerates a determined blade. It excels at one thing, which is keeping a careless mercenary alive long enough to learn caution. On every shelf, cheap, and entirely without ego.

armor.name: Mushi One
armor.special_desc: DISCRETE (You hardly register on electronic surveillance. You now always have passive concealment of 5 vs AI and Electronics.), OPT (Item can have 1 compatible option of any kind)
armor.desc: The Mushi One is for the kind of operator who would rather not be noticed at all. The field hums in tight against the skin and holds for a single hit, the gamble being entirely about when you let it take that hit; choose poorly and you're naked for the next swing. It drinks down pulse and plasma beautifully, so an energy weapon barely tickles, but a plain knife slides through the bubble with insulting ease and you'll feel every inch of the lesson. Its real party trick is staying quiet: it keeps you off the scanners that flag a walking emitter, so you read as background hum to anything watching electronically. There's room for a single custom modification, and most owners use it. Cheap, on every shelf, and quietly clever.

armor.name: Lu Corp Protect
armor.special_desc: MASTERWORK (Critical hits have no additional effects. Masterwork has no effect if the wearer is BREACHED.), NANOBOTS (During maintenance phase you can spend any number of NANITES to reroll failed AILMENTS saves.)
armor.desc: A solid mid-tier rig from Lu Corp aimed at the professional who plans to still be working next season. The field holds for five hits before it folds, rebuilding itself over a slower few beats, so it rewards measured fighting over flailing panic. Coverage is balanced and respectable, with a genuine knack for shrugging off intrusion attempts that would scramble a cheaper unit's brains. Its better trick is composure under pressure: a hit that should land somewhere vital and ruin your day instead lands as just another hit, the critical bite filed off, provided the field hasn't been breached first. Woven through it all is a maintenance swarm that lets you spend nanites to shake off lingering afflictions. Findable with a little asking, and worth the asking.

armor.name: Sukoiv III
armor.special_desc: OPT (Item can have 1 compatible option of any kind)
armor.desc: The Sukoiv III is the field you buy when most of what's being pointed at you glows. It holds for three hits with a quick couple-beat recovery between collapses, a forgiving rhythm for a working gunfighter. Against pulse and plasma it is genuinely excellent, drinking the burn so thoroughly that energy troopers find it deeply annoying. Against a hacker prying at the seams it offers almost nothing, and a blade will find the gaps with the usual indignity, so don't let anyone close. There's a slot for one custom modification, which most owners spend trying to patch that physical weak spot. Stocked widely in frontier markets, sensibly priced.

armor.name: Bellyanksky
armor.special_desc: BREAKER (Forcefield can only lose 1 charge per attack even when an attack cause multiple hits. )
armor.desc: A hard-to-find brute of a field with an enviable economy of charges. The Bellyanksky holds for three hits and snaps back almost instantly, but its real selling point is stinginess: no matter how many times a single attack lands, a burst, a flurry, a hail of fragments, it only ever costs you one hit off the count. That makes it brutally efficient against weapons designed to overwhelm. Protection is even and solid across the board rather than spectacular in any one quarter, the work of a generalist's mind. It won't dazzle the energy specialists or the hacker-hunters, but it will outlast both by simply refusing to be nickel-and-dimed to death. Seldom seen on open shelves, and the makers know exactly why you want it.

armor.name: Tac Shield
armor.special_desc: OPT (Item can have 1 compatible option of any kind)
armor.desc: A no-nonsense frontline staple, the Tac Shield does the two things a soldier actually wants and skips the brochure poetry. The field holds for three hits with a fast single-beat recovery, keeping pace with a firefight rather than lagging behind it. Where it earns its keep is breadth at the dangerous end: excellent against both steel and energy, so a trooper can take incoming rounds and a plasma bolt in the same breath without picking favorites. Intrusion and the occult get a merely adequate nod, which is fine, because the people shooting at you rarely have time for either. A single custom slot lets you tune it to taste. Hard to come by on the open market, beloved on the line.

armor.name: Exanet Aegis
armor.special_desc: AEGIS (Special modifiers to damage or power (DEADLY, DP, AS, AR and EMP etc) have no effect Vs this armor. Treat all damage at its base value.), OPT (Item can have 1 compatible option of any kind)
armor.desc: Exanet builds for the operator who treats getting hit as a planning failure and prices it accordingly. The field holds for five hits and rebuilds over a deliberate few beats, deep enough that you can stand your ground rather than dance. Energy weapons find it excellent and frustrating, intrusion attempts find it equally unwelcoming, and only steel and the occult slip past at the ordinary rate. Its prestige feature is disdain for gimmicks: armor-piercing edges, lethal modifiers, a hostile pulse meant to fry the works, all of it gets stripped down to plain damage before the field will deign to register it. A custom slot rounds out the package for the fussy. Sold in trickles to a short list, with little patience for haggling.

armor.name: Rovskaya Tactical
armor.special_desc: BREAKER (Forcefield can only lose 1 charge per attack even when an attack cause multiple hits. ), OPT (Item can have 1 compatible option of any kind)
armor.desc: The Rovskaya is a deep, miserly field for someone who intends to be standing when the smoke clears. It holds for four hits and recovers over a steady couple of beats, and like the best of its breed it refuses to be drained by volume: a multi-hit attack still costs only a single charge off the reserve, so suppressing fire wastes itself against it. Coverage is even and dependable, with a particular talent for swatting away the hacker prying at its seams. It won't win a duel against a dedicated energy lance, but it will stubbornly survive one. A custom slot invites you to shore up whichever gap worries you most. Trickled out in small batches, and steep for the privilege.

armor.name: Kraven Bioshield
armor.special_desc: INNOCULATION (Device protects against non lethal environmental hazards. Gain a LARGE bonus to skills rolls against lethal environmental hazards and ailments.)
armor.desc: A one-of-a-kind piece of living engineering that does considerably more than stop bullets. The Kraven's field holds for three hits with a brisk single-beat recovery, and across the board it offers genuinely excellent cover, energy, intrusion, and the occult all met with the same quiet competence. Its true purpose, though, is keeping the wearer breathing in places that want them dead by attrition: toxic air, hard radiation, hostile biomes. It simply shrugs off the merely unpleasant hazards, and against the lethal ones it lends a heavy helping hand in resisting poisons, plagues, and creeping afflictions. Worn more by deep-frontier survivors than by gunfighters. There is exactly one, and it is not for sale to most.

armor.name: San-Arms Racer
armor.desc: San-Arms built the Racer for the wheelman, the runner, the one who only needs the field to hold for one mad sprint. It holds for three hits and then it's done until the dust settles and the scene is over, no quick comebacks, so spend those charges like they're rent. What it does spend them on is solid: excellent at turning aside steel and incoming rounds, decent against an energy bolt, and frankly indifferent to anything subtle, with a hacker or a hex passing through almost unhindered. It is armor for the loud, fast, and forward, and useless for the patient. Findable with a little asking, cheap, and entirely honest about its narrow ambitions.

armor.name: SpecShades
armor.special_desc: OPT (Item can have 1 compatible option of any kind)
armor.desc: A serious guardian field disguised as a pair of unbothered sunglasses, which is exactly the sort of design that exceeds spec without anyone noticing. The field holds for five hits across an entire engagement before it needs the calm after to rebuild, and it covers nearly everything with genuine excellence, steel, energy, and intrusion all met with the same cool refusal. Only the stranger occult pressures get a merely adequate guard. It's the unusual bit of kit that protects like a war rig and reads like an accessory, which is precisely the point. A single custom slot lets the owner indulge a preference. Hard to come by, pricey, and far tougher than it has any right to look.

armor.name: Hyden STOPA
armor.special_desc: BREAKER (Forcefield can only lose 1 charge per attack even when an attack cause multiple hits. ), OPT (Item can have 1 compatible option of any kind)
armor.desc: The STOPA is what you build when the client is too important to be inconvenienced by physics. The field holds for an absurd ten hits across a whole engagement, and across every quarter, steel, energy, intrusion, and the occult, it doesn't merely protect, it borders on the indecent. Better still, it cannot be ground down by volume: even an attack that lands a dozen times spends only one of those ten charges, so saturation fire is a waste of perfectly good ammunition. A custom slot exists, though by the time you can afford this you can afford anything. There is one. It guards someone who matters far more than you do, and it shows.

armor.name: Nanolink Generator
armor.special_desc: OPT (Item can have 1 compatible option of any kind)
armor.desc: Unlike the bubbles you wear, the Nanolink projects its protection outward, a swarm-knit dome that can shelter more than just the one carrying it. The field holds for five hits and rebuilds over a measured few beats, with even, dependable cover across every kind of threat rather than any one specialty. It's the squad-leader's quiet insurance: plant yourself among allies and let the lattice take the edge off whatever comes for the group. Nothing about its protection dazzles, and that's deliberate, since a generalist umbrella is more useful to a team than a brilliant one over a single head. A custom slot lets you tilt it toward whatever the mission fears most. Findable with a little asking, and sensibly priced for what it spreads around.

armor.name: Tri-Net Gun Nest
armor.desc: The Tri-Net is a fixed strongpoint in a carry case, a generated dome meant to turn a doorway or a barricade into a position worth dying behind. It holds for five hits and rebuilds over a few steady beats, and at the business end it is genuinely excellent against both incoming rounds and energy fire, so a crew tucked inside can trade shots from real cover. Intrusion and the occult get the standard middling nod, which suits a thing designed for stand-up gunfights rather than ghost stories. Set it, get behind it, and make the approach expensive. Seldom on open shelves, and worth hauling for the crew that knows how to use ground.

armor.name: INW Evolved
armor.special_desc: CLOAK (Provides passive CONCEALMENT 3 type I and II. Passive concealment is 6 when not moving for a round.)
armor.desc: The pinnacle of the generator line, and one of a kind. The INW Evolved throws a dome that holds for a staggering ten hits and stitches itself back together almost as fast as it's torn, near-instant recovery making it feel less like a shield and more like a place that simply refuses to let harm in. Energy weapons find it all but impervious, and steel, intrusion, and the occult fare little better against its excellence. Its signature touch is the shimmer it lays over those it shelters: a warping veil that blurs you to eyes and sensors alike, and thickens into near-invisibility when nobody inside moves for a beat. A custom slot remains, almost as a courtesy. Singular, priceless, and very nearly unfair.

armor.name: Datacom ML4
armor.special_desc: DATACOM (The DEFENSE values of this item and its special properties is set by your DATACOM's running DEFENSE MATRIX ROUTINES. Counts as ELECTRONIC Vs EMP.)
armor.desc: Your basic datacom offering. Available just about everywhere, this unit is available in almost all shapes and sizes.

armor.name: Terminal-GO
armor.special_desc: DATACOM (The DEFENSE values of this item and its special properties is set by your DATACOM's running DEFENSE MATRIX ROUTINES. Counts as ELECTRONIC Vs EMP.), OPT (Item can have 1 compatible option of any kind)
armor.desc: Why someone would buy one of those is a mystery. Marketed towards corpos with more credits than brains.

armor.name: Model RX 66
armor.special_desc: DATACOM (The DEFENSE values of this item and its special properties is set by your DATACOM's running DEFENSE MATRIX ROUTINES. Counts as ELECTRONIC Vs EMP.)
armor.desc: A pre war design that has stood the test of time, just make sure to manage your expectations.

armor.name: Master VTK
armor.special_desc: DATACOM (The DEFENSE values of this item and its special properties is set by your DATACOM's running DEFENSE MATRIX ROUTINES. Counts as ELECTRONIC Vs EMP.)
armor.desc: The VTK is not really a hacker's datacom, it is however a fantastic option for field work when size is not a concern.

armor.name: Nanopad
armor.special_desc: DATACOM (The DEFENSE values of this item and its special properties is set by your DATACOM's running DEFENSE MATRIX ROUTINES. Counts as ELECTRONIC Vs EMP.)
armor.desc: The legendary Nanopad; amazing capabilities and a hacker's favorite. Its reputation is well established.

armor.name: Medesto
armor.special_desc: DATACOM (The DEFENSE values of this item and its special properties is set by your DATACOM's running DEFENSE MATRIX ROUTINES. Counts as ELECTRONIC Vs EMP.), OPT (Item can have 1 compatible option of any kind)
armor.desc: Medesto is one of those datacoms that doesn't quite make sense until you realize how easy it is to modify.

armor.name: Gold Board
armor.special_desc: DATACOM (The DEFENSE values of this item and its special properties is set by your DATACOM's running DEFENSE MATRIX ROUTINES. Counts as ELECTRONIC Vs EMP.)
armor.desc: Tronik tech available on the high end corpo market. Whether you trust the tech is up to you, but the power is real.

armor.name: Avatar III
armor.special_desc: DATACOM (The DEFENSE values of this item and its special properties is set by your DATACOM's running DEFENSE MATRIX ROUTINES. Counts as ELECTRONIC Vs EMP.)
armor.desc: What happens when you merge Kraven DNA with a datacom? Apparently, this thing, scary but effective.

armor.name: Hackpad
armor.special_desc: DATACOM (The DEFENSE values of this item and its special properties is set by your DATACOM's running DEFENSE MATRIX ROUTINES. Counts as ELECTRONIC Vs EMP.)
armor.desc: Immediately banned in every single alliance sector the hackpad was a commercial failure but remains the ultimate hacker status symbol.

armor.name: Godlink IV
armor.special_desc: DATACOM (The DEFENSE values of this item and its special properties is set by your DATACOM's running DEFENSE MATRIX ROUTINES. Counts as ELECTRONIC Vs EMP.)
armor.desc: The Godlink claims that it's bound to a spirit god. Whether that's true or not is debatable, what is not is just how insane the performance is.

armor.name: Model I
armor.special_desc: DATACOM (The DEFENSE values of this item and its special properties is set by your DATACOM's running DEFENSE MATRIX ROUTINES. Counts as ELECTRONIC Vs EMP.), OPT (Item can have 1 compatible option of any kind)
armor.desc: When on a budget, this datacom can do in a pinch, it will beat the snot out of most basic units, just don't expect to look cool doing it.

armor.name: Cyber Wraith
armor.special_desc: DATACOM (The DEFENSE values of this item and its special properties is set by your DATACOM's running DEFENSE MATRIX ROUTINES. Counts as ELECTRONIC Vs EMP.)
armor.desc: A black market modified datacom equipped to meet the needs of the hacker on the run.

armor.name: MBT 33
armor.special_desc: DATACOM (The DEFENSE values of this item and its special properties is set by your DATACOM's running DEFENSE MATRIX ROUTINES. Counts as ELECTRONIC Vs EMP.), OPT (Item can have 1 compatible option of any kind)
armor.desc: The MBT 33 is an experimental liquid Corinthian powered monster that provides its user with insane levels of power.

armor.name: Model III
armor.special_desc: DATACOM (The DEFENSE values of this item and its special properties is set by your DATACOM's running DEFENSE MATRIX ROUTINES. Counts as ELECTRONIC Vs EMP.), OPT (Item can have 1 compatible option of any kind)
armor.desc: Most people dismiss the Model III as a corporate tool for people that do not know any better but this datacom packs serious power and should not be underestimated.

armor.name: Datavault
armor.special_desc: DATACOM (The DEFENSE values of this item and its special properties is set by your DATACOM's running DEFENSE MATRIX ROUTINES. Counts as ELECTRONIC Vs EMP.)
armor.desc: One of the first public offerings of Tronik tech, this datacom has insane data density.

armor.name: Speed Master
armor.special_desc: DATACOM (The DEFENSE values of this item and its special properties is set by your DATACOM's running DEFENSE MATRIX ROUTINES. Counts as ELECTRONIC Vs EMP.)
armor.desc: The prized possession of many a hacker, the speed master is a staple of most top tier hackers.

armor.name: Mister Slick
armor.special_desc: DATACOM (The DEFENSE values of this item and its special properties is set by your DATACOM's running DEFENSE MATRIX ROUTINES. Counts as ELECTRONIC Vs EMP.), OPT (Item can have 1 compatible option of any kind)
armor.desc: Designed for deep corporate espionage, this datacom is custom ordered and built to exact specifications of its discerning customers.

armor.name: Vantage
armor.special_desc: DATACOM (The DEFENSE values of this item and its special properties is set by your DATACOM's running DEFENSE MATRIX ROUTINES. Counts as ELECTRONIC Vs EMP.)
armor.desc: No one thought the Speed Master could be improved upon, yet here we are.

armor.name: Hellion
armor.special_desc: DATACOM (The DEFENSE values of this item and its special properties is set by your DATACOM's running DEFENSE MATRIX ROUTINES. Counts as ELECTRONIC Vs EMP.)
armor.desc: A remodelled Hackpad for the corporate market; with more power and still super illegal, not that corporations care.

armor.name: SysM-Publix
armor.special_desc: DATACOM (The DEFENSE values of this item and its special properties is set by your DATACOM's running DEFENSE MATRIX ROUTINES. Counts as ELECTRONIC Vs EMP.)
armor.desc: The most widespread network in the galaxy. Most space stations, commercial ships and urban centers use some version of it.

armor.name: MS-1000
armor.special_desc: DATACOM (The DEFENSE values of this item and its special properties is set by your DATACOM's running DEFENSE MATRIX ROUTINES. Counts as ELECTRONIC Vs EMP.)
armor.desc: A commercial offering made from scavenged parts of the legendary MS-5000 network.

armor.name: MS-5000
armor.special_desc: DATACOM (The DEFENSE values of this item and its special properties is set by your DATACOM's running DEFENSE MATRIX ROUTINES. Counts as ELECTRONIC Vs EMP.)
armor.desc: No one remembers the origins of the MS-5000, all anyone really knows is that it dates before the Tronik uprising and survived it.

armor.name: Orion Model VII
armor.special_desc: DATACOM (The DEFENSE values of this item and its special properties is set by your DATACOM's running DEFENSE MATRIX ROUTINES. Counts as ELECTRONIC Vs EMP.)
armor.desc: The backbone of the Orion cluster. Finding one in working order today is a rare occurrence.

armor.name: Lansing Space Net
armor.special_desc: DATACOM (The DEFENSE values of this item and its special properties is set by your DATACOM's running DEFENSE MATRIX ROUTINES. Counts as ELECTRONIC Vs EMP.)
armor.desc: Lansing is known for their exquisite designs, performance and extremely limited availability.

armor.name: Nordcorp O.D.I.N
armor.special_desc: DATACOM (The DEFENSE values of this item and its special properties is set by your DATACOM's running DEFENSE MATRIX ROUTINES. Counts as ELECTRONIC Vs EMP.)
armor.desc: Little is known about Nordcorp and the O.D.I.N is rumored to be based on some Tronik tech. No one knows for sure because they've never seen one.

armor.name: Minor Farseer Barrier
armor.special_desc: BARRIER (BARRIERS increase all DEFENSES by 1 category when SPIRIT MANIFESTATION is AWAKENED or 2 when EMPOWERED.)
armor.desc: A thin veil of borrowed foresight, woven for mystics who've only just learned to feel the next breath before it lands. It hums faintly against the occult and the unseen, turning aside curses and prying spirits before they quite find their grip. Against bullets and pulse-fire it does little more than flinch politely, but a hex it simply does not believe in. The ward firms up as its bearer's focus deepens, and firmer still at the peak of their concentration. Folk-mystic work, mostly, sold cheap to acolytes who keep startling themselves by ducking blows they hadn't seen yet. Modest, but it has saved more than one card-reader from her own clientele.

armor.name: Intermediate Farseer Barrier
armor.special_desc: BARRIER (BARRIERS increase all DEFENSES by 1 category when SPIRIT MANIFESTATION is AWAKENED or 2 when EMPOWERED.)
armor.desc: A second-pupil glyph that opens behind the bearer's brow, watching the room a heartbeat ahead of everyone in it. By the time a blow lands, the wearer already half-stepped out of its line, the veil thickest against the unseen and the occult. This is the journeyman's eye, not the apprentice's squint: it reads intent, not just motion, and turns the foreknowledge into a soft refusal of harm. The ward firms as its keeper's spirit gathers, and firms again at the crest of their focus, like a prediction that grows more certain the longer you watch the dice. It will not tell you what you want to know. It will only make sure you survive learning it.

armor.name: Major Farseer Barrier
armor.special_desc: BARRIER (BARRIERS increase all DEFENSES by 1 category when SPIRIT MANIFESTATION is AWAKENED or 2 when EMPOWERED.)
armor.desc: They say the master who first wove this one stopped flinching years before she ever put it on, because she had already seen every blow that would land. A pale lattice of foresight rides a half-second ahead of the body, leaning hardest against the things that come for the soul, where the future is murkiest and most worth knowing. It is no fortress against bullet or flame, but against the unseen it is patient and sure. As its bearer's spirit wakes, the lattice widens its gaze and every guard rises with it; at the full flood of power it reads the room before the room exists. A relic of the old Berilia school, copied a thousand times and never once equaled.

armor.name: Minor Entropy Barrier
armor.special_desc: BARRIER (BARRIERS increase all DEFENSES by 1 category when SPIRIT MANIFESTATION is AWAKENED or 2 when EMPOWERED.)
armor.desc: Rather than block harm, this nascent field invites it to simply fall apart on the way in. Spiritual assaults lose their thread and unravel into harmless static; blade and beam it dulls only a little, but the occult it actively forgets. It is a quiet thing, the dim grey shimmer of a working that prefers decay to defiance. The veil hardens as its wearer's spirit stirs, sharper yet at full focus, though even then it never quite stops looking tired. A favorite of patient, unglamorous adepts who'd rather a threat dissolve than be fought. Cheap, grim, and oddly soothing to watch.

armor.name: Intermediate Entropy Barrier
armor.special_desc: BARRIER (BARRIERS increase all DEFENSES by 1 category when SPIRIT MANIFESTATION is AWAKENED or 2 when EMPOWERED.)
armor.desc: Everything decays, and this developed working has simply learned to point that decay outward — incoming force unravels into heat and rust before it can finish arriving. Edges go dull, charges fizzle, momentum sighs and lies down a few centimeters short of the wearer's skin. It is a hungry, patient field, absorbing up a great deal of punishment with the bored confidence of something that has watched stars burn out. Against ward-cracking and physical battery it is especially fond, dismantling them into the dust they were always going to become. The ward strengthens as the keeper's spirit rises, and more at the peak of their focus. It does not stop the heat-death of the universe. It just makes sure you're not first in line.

armor.name: Major Entropy Barrier
armor.special_desc: BARRIER (BARRIERS increase all DEFENSES by 1 category when SPIRIT MANIFESTATION is AWAKENED or 2 when EMPOWERED.)
armor.desc: Everything frays — this ward simply volunteers to fray first, and forever. Cast as a slow grey dissolution around the bearer, it drinks the momentum out of harm until even a furious strike arrives as a tired suggestion. It is gentlest at the surface and merciless at depth, absorbing up an extraordinary measure of punishment before it so much as flickers. As the wearer's spirit stirs the decay spreads outward to every guard at once, and when their power crests, attacks seem to age and crumble in the air. Mystics call it honest: it promises only that all things end, and keeps the promise on your enemies first.

armor.name: Minor Destiny Barrier
armor.special_desc: BARRIER (BARRIERS increase all DEFENSES by 1 category when SPIRIT MANIFESTATION is AWAKENED or 2 when EMPOWERED.), ABSOLUTION (You get maximum SOAK when a critical faillure results in a SOAK roll. (From a DEFENSE check or other checks))
armor.desc: A small wager with fate, stitched into a ward that pays out worst when you stumble. The veil leans toward the occult and the unseen, fending off hexes and hungry spirits more reliably than steel or plasma. Its strange grace is in the fumble: at your most graceless, most catastrophic moment, the field holds its absolute firmest, as if luck only respects you when you've stopped trying to impress it. The ward also tightens as its bearer's spirit stirs, and tighter still at full focus. Uncommon, a touch pricey, and beloved by gamblers, fools, and the chronically clumsy. It rewards the kind of person who survives precisely because they keep tripping into safety.

armor.name: Intermediate Destiny Barrier
armor.special_desc: BARRIER (BARRIERS increase all DEFENSES by 1 category when SPIRIT MANIFESTATION is AWAKENED or 2 when EMPOWERED.), ABSOLUTION (You get maximum SOAK when a critical faillure results in a SOAK roll. (From a DEFENSE check or other checks))
armor.desc: Woven by a mystic who decided the dice owed them, this seasoned ward feeds on the worst possible moment. When a guard fails most catastrophically — the fumble, the slip, the instant everything goes wrong — the field reaches its absolute fullness, turning the clumsiest beat into its finest hour. The protection it offers in a clean fight is solid and confident, leaning toward the spiritual; the protection it offers in disaster is something closer to a miracle with a smug grin. It hardens as the bearer's spirit gathers and hardens further at the apex of their focus. Fixers out of Berilia sell these to people who attract calamity. They are, unsurprisingly, very expensive and very popular.

armor.name: Major Destiny Barrier
armor.special_desc: BARRIER (BARRIERS increase all DEFENSES by 1 category when SPIRIT MANIFESTATION is AWAKENED or 2 when EMPOWERED.), ABSOLUTION (You get maximum SOAK when a critical faillure results in a SOAK roll. (From a DEFENSE check or other checks))
armor.desc: Most wards protect you on your good days; this one was built for the worst instant of your life. A thread of fixed fate runs through it, so that the exact moment your hands betray you and everything goes wrong becomes, perversely, the moment it holds like a closed fist — absolute, unbreakable, no roll of the bones required. Against the spiritual it is already a deep and certain shield, and it lifts every other guard higher as the bearer's spirit wakes, to something like inevitability at the height of their power. They tell of duelists who fumbled, certain they were dead, and walked away untouched. Fate, it turns out, can be bought — though the price would buy a moon.

armor.name: Minor Ironmind Barrier
armor.special_desc: BARRIER (BARRIERS increase all DEFENSES by 1 category when SPIRIT MANIFESTATION is AWAKENED or 2 when EMPOWERED.), MOTIVATING (You have maximum SOAK value against MORALE attacks)
armor.desc: A nascent ward built less for the body than for the resolve behind it. It leans toward the spiritual, blunting curses and creeping dread, though blades and pulse-fire pass it with only mild complaint. Its true gift is against words and fear: every attempt to break your nerve, shame you, or talk you into despair simply slides off at its weakest. The veil grows stronger as its bearer's spirit stirs, stronger still at the height of their focus. Cheap, common acolyte gear, the sort issued to nervous initiates who must learn to stand in a hostile room and not flinch. It will not make you brave, but it will make you look it.

armor.name: Intermediate Ironmind Barrier
armor.special_desc: BARRIER (BARRIERS increase all DEFENSES by 1 category when SPIRIT MANIFESTATION is AWAKENED or 2 when EMPOWERED.), MOTIVATING (You have maximum SOAK value against MORALE attacks)
armor.desc: Fear, dread, and the slow rot of demoralization break against this developed ward like surf against a sea wall that has stopped being impressed. Against anything aimed at the spirit's resolve, it gives its absolute best every single time — no flinch, no wavering, the keeper's nerve held at full regardless of how ugly the room gets. The wider veil leans into the occult and unseen, dependable rather than dazzling. It firms as its bearer's spirit rises and firms again at the height of their focus. Mercenaries call it the workhorse for negotiations that go sideways. It will not make you brave. It will simply make 'terrified' a purely private experience.

armor.name: Major Ironmind Barrier
armor.special_desc: BARRIER (BARRIERS increase all DEFENSES by 1 category when SPIRIT MANIFESTATION is AWAKENED or 2 when EMPOWERED.), MOTIVATING (You have maximum SOAK value against MORALE attacks)
armor.desc: Despair is just another weapon, and this veil treats it like one. Whatever venom is poured into the ear or the heart — the taunt, the terror, the slow erosion of will — it meets a will already settled at its absolute peak, immovable, every doubt absorbed away to nothing. The body it guards is only modestly armored against steel and fire, but the mind behind it cannot be made to break. As the bearer's spirit rises the calm spreads outward to every guard, becoming, at full power, a serenity that borders on rude. Inquisitors of the Order covet it; ironically, it makes its wearer impervious to inquisition.

armor.name: Minor Misfortune Barrier
armor.special_desc: BARRIER (BARRIERS increase all DEFENSES by 1 category when SPIRIT MANIFESTATION is AWAKENED or 2 when EMPOWERED.), ENTROPIC (This defense gains a MINIMUM SOAK value equal to the RAW CHI pool. This value cannot exceed the maximum SOAK value.)
armor.desc: A sullen little field that draws its strength straight from the bearer's inner well — the deeper their reserve runs, the more harm it flatly refuses to allow. It tilts toward the occult, smothering hexes and spirit-strikes more than bullet or beam. On a hollow, depleted day it is merely adequate; on a full one it becomes stubborn, setting a floor of protection beneath even the worst luck. The ward also firms as its wearer's spirit stirs, harder yet at full focus. Rare and dear, the work of secretive ascetics who hoard their energy like misers. The catch, of course, is that you must actually have something in the tank.

armor.name: Intermediate Misfortune Barrier
armor.special_desc: BARRIER (BARRIERS increase all DEFENSES by 1 category when SPIRIT MANIFESTATION is AWAKENED or 2 when EMPOWERED.), ENTROPIC (This defense gains a MINIMUM SOAK value equal to the RAW CHI pool. This value cannot exceed the maximum SOAK value.)
armor.desc: Tuned by a self-taught mystic who treated bad luck as a renewable resource, this ward draws its floor of protection from the bearer's own inner well — the deeper that reserve runs, the more harm it flatly refuses, up to the limit of the field's own considerable strength. On its own it already turns aside a punishing amount, the kind of veil that makes attackers double-check their math. Pair it with a full spirit and it becomes a guarantee dressed as a curse on everyone else. It thickens as the keeper's spirit gathers, and thickens further at the crest of their focus. The catch is honest: an empty soul gets the baseline and nothing more. Misfortune, it turns out, is mostly other people's.

armor.name: Major Misfortune Barrier
armor.special_desc: BARRIER (BARRIERS increase all DEFENSES by 1 category when SPIRIT MANIFESTATION is AWAKENED or 2 when EMPOWERED.), ENTROPIC (This defense gains a MINIMUM SOAK value equal to the RAW CHI pool. This value cannot exceed the maximum SOAK value.)
armor.desc: A masterwork of bottomless cruelty to anyone foolish enough to strike at a deep soul. This ward draws a floor of protection straight from the bearer's own inner reserve — the vaster their well of spirit, the more harm it flatly forbids before a single die is cast, up to the staggering ceiling it already commands. Against a shallow vessel it is merely excellent; against a true master it becomes a wall that bad luck builds higher the harder you hit it. Every other guard lifts as the spirit wakes, and at the crest of power the wearer simply stops being a thing that misfortune can find. One of a kind, and the kind of thing wars are quietly fought over.

armor.name: Minor Sustenance Barrier
armor.special_desc: BARRIER (BARRIERS increase all DEFENSES by 1 category when SPIRIT MANIFESTATION is AWAKENED or 2 when EMPOWERED.), SPACE (Device is rated for space and provides up to 8 hours of life support as well as magnetic boots. Treat character as having GRAVITY TRAINING when walking on compatible surfaces.)
armor.desc: A practical traveler's ward, equal parts mysticism and life-support. It leans spiritual, turning aside the occult and the unseen better than blade or plasma, but its real selling point is keeping you breathing where there is nothing to breathe. The field seals against vacuum for a working day, and grips compatible hull-plating so the wearer strides across the void as if born to it. The veil also strengthens as its bearer's spirit stirs, stronger still at full focus. Common dockside enchantment, favored by frontier salvagers who'd rather not choose between a warded soul and a working airlock. Mystics call it inelegant; the people walking on the outside of ships call it indispensable.

armor.name: Intermediate Sustenance Barrier
armor.special_desc: BARRIER (BARRIERS increase all DEFENSES by 1 category when SPIRIT MANIFESTATION is AWAKENED or 2 when EMPOWERED.), SPACE (Device is rated for space and provides up to 8 hours of life support as well as magnetic boots. Treat character as having GRAVITY TRAINING when walking on compatible surfaces.)
armor.desc: A practical mystic's working, this seasoned veil keeps a body breathing where bodies are not meant to breathe — rated for the void, good for the better part of a working shift in vacuum, with a whisper of magnetism that lets the wearer walk a hull like a deck. The wider field leans spiritual and reliable, absorbing a healthy share of incoming harm while it quietly handles the unglamorous business of air and footing. It firms as the bearer's spirit rises and firms again at the peak of their focus. Frontier salvagers swear by it; it has opinions about which surfaces are 'compatible' and will let you discover the others the hard way. Keep you alive in the black. That is the whole pitch, and it delivers.

armor.name: Major Sustenance Barrier
armor.special_desc: BARRIER (BARRIERS increase all DEFENSES by 1 category when SPIRIT MANIFESTATION is AWAKENED or 2 when EMPOWERED.), SPACE (Device is rated for space and provides up to 8 hours of life support as well as magnetic boots. Treat character as having GRAVITY TRAINING when walking on compatible surfaces.)
armor.desc: Apex spirit-craft that thought to ask the rude question: what good is a ward if the void kills you anyway? This one sheathes the bearer in a self-renewing shell that breathes for them in the airless dark, holds them to any deck through the worst tumble, and walks them across a hull as if the spinning station had manners. Its protection is profound and steady, deepest against the occult, lifting every guard as the bearer's spirit stirs and climbing absurdly high at full flood. Frontier wardens swear by it; salvage crews swear at the price. Either way, the vacuum has lost a reliable customer.

armor.name: Minor Gambling Barrier
